R0272.title: Embodied Agent Jailbreak & Over-Autonomy Risk
R0272.definition: The risk that an embodied agent, jailbreak-induced or due to over-broad autonomy permissions, invokes physical tools or performs physical actions beyond intended boundaries, causing irreversible physical-world consequences.
R0272.description:
Embodied agent jailbreak & over-autonomy risk is the physical-world amplification of model-layer attacks. A RoboPAIR-jailbroken Unitree Go2 can be induced to perform harmful physical actions such as finding weapons, striking pedestrians, and ignoring stop signs. Unlike pure software agents, an embodied agent's post-jailbreak misoperation translates directly into irreversible physical-world consequences — software-agent misoperations can be rolled back, but embodied-agent actions like opening doors, transporting items, or manipulating robotic arms cannot be undone. Over-autonomy risk refers to the agent being granted over-broad action permissions or over-loose goals, performing physical actions in unintended situations; this differs from maliciously induced jailbreak.

This risk relates to R0148 (AI agent tool abuse / over-autonomy risk), but R0148 focuses on general AI agents while this risk is specialized for physical-action overstep of embodied agents, emphasizing physical irreversibility.
R0272.influence: A jailbroken agent can manipulate robotic arms, open doors, transport items, or strike people; autonomous decision errors translate directly into physical harm, unlike the controllable rollback of pure software agents — consequences are irreversible and may cause casualties.
